chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi and Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
regarding a woman who breast-fed the son of her slave girl: 'She emancipates him.'

key_terms.أَرْضَعَتِ: She breast-fed; the act of nursing that creates legal milk-kinship (radha'ah)
key_terms.تُعْتِقُهُ: She emancipates him; manumission, the legal freeing of a slave
key_terms.جَارِيَة: Slave girl; a female slave owned by the woman

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling if a woman breast-feeds her slave girl's child?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) issued a legal ruling that if a free woman breast-feeds the son of her own slave girl, the act of nursing creates a bond that obligates the emancipation of that child. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that wet-nursing can establish milk-kinship (radha'ah) with legal consequences, and that the breast-feeding of a slave's child by the slave's owner creates a legal obligation of manumission. In the classical Islamic context, the Imam's audience would have understood this as an application of both the laws of wet-nursing and the laws governing the freedom of slaves.
